signal_jp_mesh — DRIVE roadjp op

• Data kinds: none → table (an op determined by its arguments alone — it takes no image or data input)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.signal_jp_mesh(*, lens: 'float' = 0.3, n: 'int' = 3, hood: 'bool' = True, state: 'str' = 'off') -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import roadjp; roadjp.signal_jp_mesh(*, lens: 'float' = 0.3, n: 'int' = 3, hood: 'bool' = True, state: 'str' = 'off') -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("signal_jp_mesh"))

Usage

Horizontal vehicle signal head (Japanese style). Origin = center of the bottom face of the signal head; the display face points to −x.

Box: width = n·(lens + 0.10) + 0.05(1.25 m with 3 lights and 300 mm), height = lens + 0.13(0.43 m), depth 0.30 m, dark gray. Lens = Place a disk (24 divisions) with radius lens/2 5 mm outside the front surface (−x side). The order is blue, yellow, red from +y to −y. When you look at the display surface facing −x from the front, +y is on the right, so the colors are blue, yellow, and red from the right. If n = 2, it will be yellow/red, if n = 1, it will be yellow (single flashing type). Eaves (thin box, 0.25 m long, hood) above each lens. The lens diameter is 300 mm (standard 250 mm since 2017, both currently in use).

Returns {"V", "F", "color", "label": 3, "lamp_faces": {"green": (f0, f1), ...}, "width", "height", "depth", "lens"}. lamp_faces is the index range of the faces in this mesh (when adding to the world, translate to the range returned by world_add — Same mechanism as driveworld.add_signal). Only the lights in state have the driveworld._LAMP color, the others have the "off" color.
